### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `81f65b36f6ecca3c12f079295cacf6d0cf6b443c` — the merge of head `af2b6b3f339361b216bac0fefbb17330f9c41f4d` into base `00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 81f65b36f6ecca3c12f079295cacf6d0cf6b443c && git checkout 81f65b36f6ecca3c12f079295cacf6d0cf6b443c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b af2b6b3f339361b216bac0fefbb17330f9c41f4d && git checkout -B drift-repro 00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b && git merge --no-ff af2b6b3f339361b216bac0fefbb17330f9c41f4d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 00d0668d380046198dfc9151858b88df463bfd9b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af2b6b3f339361b216bac0fefbb17330f9c41f4d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/record-page-routes.ts (`answerTimeline`, `readStream`), packages/spec/src/data/feed.zod.ts (`SYS_ACTIVITY_BUILTIN_TYPES`), ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts (`ACTIVITY_TYPE_TO_FEED_TYPE`, `applyFeedConfig`), ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/recordTimelineStream.ts (`mergeTimelineStream`, `auditEntriesToFeedItems`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx (the page's `timeline` plan, its `sys_comment` and `sys_audit_log` reads), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts (`action` values), packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-page-timeline.dogfood.test.ts

Inputs: card #28737 (body and its 4 comments, the os-dev-report 6570130917 included), PR #28991 body and file list, the net diff against `main` at the head, and the head's check-runs as of 2026-11-02T05:58Z: 27 completed success, 7 skipped, 33 still in progress (Test Core 8 shards, Test UI 16 shards, Type Check ×3, Build ×3, Lint UI, Live E2E UI, Build & E2E UI), 0 failed. The green ones that bear on this face: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards. The lane seat lands only on the fully green head, as the queue guard requires.

### ① Derived judgments

- `RecordPageRequestSchema` gains `timeline?: RecordPageTimelineRequestSchema` (strict, three required booleans). An optional member on a strict object widens the accept set and refuses nothing a `main` client sends: **right**. The strictness (a `timeline: true`, a missing source, an extra key are 400) is pinned in the spec test and the route test: **right**.
- `RecordPageResponseSchema` gains `timeline?: RecordPageTimelineCountSchema | RecordPageStreamRefusalSchema` (`{ total: int ≥ 0 }` strict, or `{ error }`). Optional, same refusal shape as the other stream parts (#28470): **right**. `{ total, error }` and `{ total, records }` refused by the test: **right**.
- Four new exports from `@objectstack/spec/api`: the two schemas with their `X`/`XParsed` types, `RECORD_TIMELINE_UNDRAWN_ACTIVITY_TYPES` (`as const satisfies readonly SysActivityBuiltinType[]`) and `RECORD_TIMELINE_UPDATE_ACTIVITY_TYPE`. Additive; the type-only import from `../data/feed.zod` follows the existing api→data imports (analytics.zod.ts, batch.zod.ts, contract.zod.ts): **right**. The test pins every undrawn type as a built-in and `updated` as not undrawn: **right**.
- `RECORD_PAGE_MAX_ACTIVITY_ROWS` stays 200 and `RecordPageActivityRequestSchema` keeps `1..200`: no narrowing, as the card's scope note and the claim ruled: **right**. The docblock's wording moves the count's ownership to the `timeline` part: **right**.
- Five regenerated spec artifacts (api-surface, authorable-surface, declaration-map, export-origins, json-schema.manifest) carry the four exports; Spec property liveness and the repo gates are green on the head: **right**.
- The first consumer (`answerTimeline`) reads each source with `findData` as the caller, behind the stream object's exposure gate via `readStream`, with `limit: 0, count: true`. That is the route's own related-list pattern (`limit: entry.top, count: true`, `top` min 0) and `total` falls back to `records.length` only when the driver answers no total: **right**. `$nin` is a declared filter operator (`analytics.zod.ts`, `field.test.ts`): **right**.
- `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` on a source counts 0 (an unregistered `sys_audit_log` on a boot without plugin-audit) while a refused comment or activity read refuses the part and a refused ledger read counts 0. That is the console's own asymmetry: `RecordDetailView` catches and warns on a failed `sys_audit_log` read and draws no field change, but surfaces `commentsDenied`/`activityDenied`: **right**, and the spec prose says it.
- `FIELD_CHANGE_ACTIONS = ['create','update','delete']` against `sys_audit_log.action`'s twelve values (`read`, `login`, `import`, `action_invocation`, … among them): the writes are the rows that carry a before/after the stream can draw: **right**.
- `@object-ui/types` `RecordPagePayload.timeline?` optional: **right**. No `ui/.changeset` entry, as #28682 (16 ui files) landed without one and Check Changeset is green: **right**.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28737-record-page-timeline-count.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/rest` minor; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: added`. The diff publishes exactly a widening (new optional request and response members, new exports, a new served part on `POST /api/v1/data/{object}/{id}/page`) and no narrowing. The PR body carries the same two lines. Check Changeset and check-changeset-no-major green on the head. **Matches.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `open_questions` block and no dev flag on the PR body or the report. The body's Acceptance notes name one known drift (the console draws a ledger row only with a displayable diff, and reads 50): answered under ④ as should-fix ④-1, which asks the spec prose to carry it.
- Skills-docs: none. Checked: no `skills/**` file teaches the record page payload's parts; `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx` and the regenerated reference page are prose, left to the lane seat.
- Serial constraint with #28483 (seat 1): on `main` and merged into this branch; the report's re-verification at the merged head stands.
- Tier H: 1366 changed lines, not crossed. Governed Surface Queue Guard green.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts`, judged against card #28737's Wanted 1 ("the server's own count of the same merged stream the panel draws, with the panel's type exclusions") and its first consumer (`answerTimeline`, then the console's chip, 「查看全部 N 条」, the 动态 tab count and the tab-row probe through `RecordTimelineTotalContext`).

The contract holds. The timeline table defines the count by rows, source by source, with the one subtraction `mergeTimelineStream` makes (the `updated` activity rows when any field change is counted), and the route computes exactly that table; the dogfood suite proves it equal to the separate `$count` reads as the same member on a real boot with plugin-audit's writers. The "one definition" for the dropped types is real: `ACTIVITY_TYPE_TO_FEED_TYPE` now builds its `undefined` rows from the spec constant and `mergeTimelineStream` uses the update constant, so a type added to one side cannot be missed on the other. I tried the breaks the card invites: a record with more than 200 activity rows (the count no longer saturates); a reply (counted on both sides: the tab draws replies as items, the peek names roots only but reports `all.items.length`); a source the boot does not register (0, as the page reads an empty stream); the comment thread written to after open (the console swaps the payload's comment count for the comments it holds); a refused ledger read (0 on both sides). None breaks.

- **should-fix ④-1 (prose in the `hits` file, no schema change).** The docblock at lines 70–77 ("The one definition … Every other value … is an entry") and the table at 156–176 read as if the count equals the drawn stream. Two console rules the table does not carry make the drawn stream smaller than the count, never larger: (a) `applyFeedConfig` hides a `completed` activity (`task` kind) unless the panel sets `showCompleted`, the row is a milestone or a logged interaction; the server cannot tell those rows apart without reading each row's metadata, so it counts every `completed` row; (b) `auditEntriesToFeedItems` draws a ledger write only when `collectAuditChanges` finds a displayable diff, and the console reads the newest 50. The PR body's Acceptance notes name (b) and not (a). Write both into the `RecordPageTimelineRequestSchema` docblock (one sentence after "The total is their sum."): the count is the sources' rows as this table defines them; the panel's own display configuration (`showCompleted`, `types`) and a ledger row with nothing displayable draw fewer, so the count is an upper bound of the drawn entries and equal to them on the default panel without completed tasks. A reader of the spec then knows what `total` is and is not, which is the point of declaring it first. Not a must-fix: the contract as written is exact, testable and pinned, the card's own scenarios hold, and the consumer's chip was already computed over a different row set than the tab draws before this PR.
- Read, not a finding: when both `activity` and `fieldChanges` are named the `updates` count is read in parallel even when `changes` turns out 0 and it is not used. One read per page open on a record without field changes; sequencing it would add a round trip to the common case, so the parallel read is the right trade.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-6jkgb1`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jV5sBSzCYNEDgpYLJw`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Should-fix ④-1 is prose in the schema file; if the seat takes it on this branch before landing, the head moves on a prose-only hunk and carries under `Regen-provenance:`/prose carry rules; if it lands as is, the seat files it as a follow-up with this comment as the reference.

The refused-ledger case is pinned in the rest unit test only.
